task: Find bribery and corruption enforcement involving Ericsson, including its deferred prosecution agreement

key.question: Which legal entity is the subject, and what is its group and HQ? Which group entities were charged?
key.answer: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ), Stockholm, Sweden. It is the listed parent. Swedish org. no. 556016-0680 (from memory, not re-checked). In the 2019 resolution the parent signed the DPA. Subsidiary Ericsson (Egypt) Ltd pleaded guilty to conspiracy to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions. Ericsson Inc. (US) is a separate group entity. It is a co-defendant in the Iraq terrorism civil suit, not in the DOJ case.

key.question: What was the original December 2019 FCPA resolution: conduct, countries, amount and structure?
key.answer: On 6 Dec 2019 Ericsson resolved DOJ and SEC FCPA charges for about $1.06bn in total. The DOJ criminal penalty was about $520.7M. The SEC disgorgement was about $540M. The conduct was bribes, slush funds and false books and records in Djibouti, China, Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait, from 2000 to 2016. The parent entered a three-year DPA with an independent compliance monitor. Ericsson Egypt pleaded guilty.

key.question: Did Ericsson breach the DPA, and what was the consequence?
key.answer: Yes. In March 2022 the DOJ determined that Ericsson had breached the DPA by failing to disclose enough about its internal Iraq investigation (2011–2019), including possible payments to terrorist groups. In March 2023 Ericsson pleaded guilty to two counts: conspiracy to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions and conspiracy to violate the books-and-records provisions. It agreed to pay about $206.7M more. The DPA ended through the plea. The monitorship and reporting were extended to June 2024.

key.question: Is the DOJ obligation / monitorship still running today?
key.answer: No. Ericsson announced the monitorship concluded in June 2024. The March 2023 plea agreement's term expired on about 2 June 2024. No DOJ or SEC FCPA obligation is open. Compliance Week reports the compliance programme as a post-settlement success. Reputational and recidivism risk remains. I found no later DOJ breach finding.

key.question: What is still open on the Iraq conduct (alleged payments to ISIS/al-Qaeda, Feb 2022 ICIJ leak)?
key.answer: Ericsson's internal investigation, which found serious breaches of compliance rules and apparent corruption in Iraq, has no announced completion timeline as of 2023. I found no 2024–26 update on whether it is closed. I found no Swedish prosecution. A Swedish-language check ("Ericsson åklagare Irak") is still needed. Ericsson denies that it can show money reached terrorist groups.

key.question: What major civil litigation is pending from the Iraq allegations?
key.answer: Schmitz et al. v. Ericsson Inc. et al., No. 1:22-cv-02317 (D.D.C.), is an Anti-Terrorism Act suit. It was filed in 2022 by hundreds of US victims' families and is still pending as far as I found. A merits ruling is unconfirmed, so check the docket. Related insurance cases found Travelers and Ace owed Ericsson no defence in two ATA suits (affirmed on appeal). The US securities and derivative suit over the Iraq disclosures was dismissed.

key.question: Excluded namesakes, and what screening was done?
key.answer: Candidates to exclude include Ericsson Egypt (included, as a group entity), unrelated persons or firms named Ericsson or Ericson, and the Ericsson-LG joint venture. Only the Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson group matches the DPA. My search found no sanctions or PEP hits tied to the parent. A formal sanctions-list check was not run.
